designDecisions.decision: New file report-manifest.ts. ReportManifest = { product, sections: ReadonlyArray<ReportSectionId> } where ReportSectionId is a closed string-literal union. No index signature, so an object literal assigned to ReportManifest with an extra fact-shaped property fails TS excess-property-check at compile time -- verified by a real @ts-expect-error fixture in a type-test file, not a narrated claim. All four manifests (site-plan, x-ray, flood, feasibility) are defined per the WDLL's own 'shape' section, but only FEASIBILITY_MANIFEST gets a real renderer this round; the other three exist as data + are used to prove R1's identity property without cutting X-Ray/Site Plan/Flood over (that stays R6/R7).

New file report-model.ts. ParcelReportModel = { parcelNodeId, geometry: FeasibilityFactState<SitePlanModel>, facts: {...}, drainage: FeasibilityFactState<FloodDrainageStudy>, package: PackageLayer }. Reuses the existing per-section fact interfaces from feasibility-model.ts (JurisdictionFacts, ParcelOwnershipFacts, etc.) rather than reinventing them -- they already satisfy R1's 'present/absent with provenance' requirement. Two-layer composition mirrors the existing author.ts pattern (composeSitePlanModelForParcel already split from the authors that call it): composeParcelReportFacts(sitePlan, storage, ...) is the atoms-driven half (today's composeFeasibilityModel, extended with drainage+package), composeParcelReport(parcelNodeId, options) = composeSitePlanModelForParcel + composeParcelReportFacts, for the full orchestration R1 describes. R1's identity check is proven by two independent section-reader functions (used by two different manifests, including a not-fully-wired X_RAY_MANIFEST) pulling the SAME model.facts.* object reference via toBe, not toEqual -- without cutting X-Ray's real PDF over.

geometry composition wrapped: on throw, geometry becomes absent(sitePlanUnavailableFromError(error).summary) instead of the whole report throwing (feasibility-author.ts currently hard-throws here -- this is the exact behavior being generalized, described in the dispatch as 'tonight's outage fix generalised'). Atoms fetch wrapped once; a fetch failure makes every atom-derived section (parcelOwnership, flood, specialDistricts, wellsPipelines, footprint) absent with the SAME honestly-shared reason rather than pretending independence. Each section's own derivation additionally gets its own try/catch for a malformed-atom-shape fault. utilities/dischargePoint keep their existing per-call try/catch. terrain becomes FeasibilityFactState-shaped since it depends on geometry. package computation is defensively coded and wrapped with a minimal absent-flavored fallback so a synthesis bug can't take down the whole document either. Verified by violation: a new test suite forces each section to throw in turn (stubbed storage/resolver) and asserts the OTHER sections still resolve and the document composes.

Field deleted outright from FloodFacts, ComposeFeasibilityModelOptions-successor, AuthorParcelFeasibilityExportOptions, and the route's zod body schema (feasibilityRefreshBody) -- not renamed, not deprecated. drainage: FeasibilityFactState<FloodDrainageStudy> becomes its own top-level model field, resolved by: (1) look up the shared parcel-terrain-model atom's json-flood-drainage-study artifact (already written today by flood-drainage-author.ts -- real existing infra, not new); (2) if present and generatedAt is within a documented staleness TTL, read+parse it (present, no compute cost); (3) else, ONLY if the caller opts in (resolveDrainage.runWhenStale: true plus run inputs), run runFloodDrainageStudy fresh and persist the result onto the same atom/artifact store, mirroring authorParcelFloodDrainageReport's own persistence shape; (4) absent with reason otherwise. No staleness convention exists anywhere else in this codebase for this study -- I'm introducing one explicitly (documented constant, not silently assumed) since the card requires 'runs when stale' but names no TTL; flagged as a reversible default in my close.
designDecisions.whyOptIn: Making drainage resolution opt-in (rather than automatic inside every composeParcelReport call) is the direct, proactive answer to the dispatch's own named risk: 'if composing the whole model... costs materially more and caching does not close it, STOP and report.' Opt-in means existing/cheap callers (and every existing unit test) pay zero extra cost by default; the real production Feasibility route opts in explicitly, matching today's Flood-Drainage report's own real-network default. This also avoids silently turning every existing feasibility-author.test.ts case into a live-network test.

designDecisions.decision: pdf/feasibility.ts's entry point moves from FeasibilityModel to ParcelReportModel + FEASIBILITY_MANIFEST. Package-layer computation (verdict headline, open items, data-quality note, deterministic narrative skeleton) MOVES from pdf/feasibility.ts + feasibility-model.ts into report-model.ts's package composition, since R5 says this must be 'computed across all sections rather than one product's slice' (today's generateOpenItems/deterministicNarrative only see feasibility-model fields, never drainage). narrativeOverride (LLM-generated) threading stays at the author/PDF layer exactly as today -- it is request-scoped and side-effecting, not part of a cacheable composition. Drainage section (flood-cover/catchment/ponding/flow-paths) renders the REAL study honestly present/absent instead of the caller-boolean-driven 'Site-specific drainage study: On file' chip. Geometry-absent path: header falls back to caller-supplied descriptor address/countyName (mirrors dossier-author.ts's existing pattern for the same situation), zoning-envelope section renders a declared-absent block, appended site-plan sheet is simply omitted -- all mechanisms that already exist elsewhere in this codebase, applied here rather than invented.

preRegisteredSelfChecks: Could composeParcelReport's atoms-fetch failure be mistaken for genuine per-atom absence? Guarded against by giving the fetch-failure path its own distinct reason string ('... read failed: <message>') vs the not-found path's ('No X atom on file for this parcel') -- a test asserts the two reasons are textually distinguishable.

Could making drainage opt-in silently mean production Feasibility never actually gets a real study (looks fixed, isn't)? Guarded against by wiring the actual engine-api route to pass resolveDrainage.runWhenStale: true using the SAME resolver/fetchDem the route already has for site-plan, and by live-verifying against a real parcel post-implementation rather than trusting the unit tests alone.
